english.title: Loan to another / allow to be used by another a CPC / other document
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to deceive, lent to, or allowed to be used by, **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a document as referred to in regulation 11(2) of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007, namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT..), providing evidence of a CPC
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 13(1)(b) and (4) of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.

english.notes:
(i) In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, "forges" means makes a false document in order that it may be used as genuine.
(ii) See regulation 13(5), (6), (7) and (8) for details in relation to the time limits on prosecutions.
(iii) See regulation 14 for the power to seize documents.
(iv) This offence applies from the 3rd December 2024 due to changes made by SI 2024/1160 to the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007. For the offences applying before this date, see H20126 (document / qualification card / community licence / certificate) and H21545 (Swiss CPC / other document).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Complex - see regulation 13 of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
